+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '80'
+title: 'CI: always run a real integration suite (nested IntegrationTests package), like the sibling libraries'
+---
+## Problem
+CI never runs integration tests. The `unit / Integration (opt-in, real dependencies)` job is `skipped` on each run (for example run 38306818520 for 47eadc2). Commit 24643be deleted `IntegrationTests/Package.swift` and the `integration-package-path` input, and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` now says "there is no integration package". Only a stale `IntegrationTests/Package.resolved` is left. The sibling libraries (FoundationModelsACP, FoundationModelsExtras, FoundationModelsKanban, FoundationModelsACPAgent) all run integration on each push. The user requires the same here.
+
+## Contract
+Obey `swissarmyhammer/workflows/docs/swift-ci.md` (local copy: `../workflows/docs/swift-ci.md`), Shape 2:
+- `swift test` at the root runs only unit tests.
+- The nested package `IntegrationTests/Package.swift` depends on the root package by `.package(path: "..")`. The root manifest does not name it.
+- No environment variable selects a test.
+- `ci.yml` gives `integration-package-path: IntegrationTests` to the shared `swift-ci.yaml`. Add `integration-no-parallel: true` if the tests start processes or load a model. Add `integration-metallib-glob: "*Cmlx*/default.metallib"` if the graph includes MLX (FoundationModelsExtras does; see the Extras and Kanban `ci.yml`).
+- Rewrite the header comment of `ci.yml` to describe this, in the same style as `../FoundationModelsKanban/.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
+
+## The integration suite
+The suite must use a real agent with a real model through the public API of this library. This is the purpose of the library. Use `../FoundationModelsACPAgent` as the agent. Its `IntegrationTests/Package.swift` shows how it depends on the sibling packages by `branch: main`, and how it handles MLX (`MetalLibraryTestBootstrap` in FoundationModelsRouter). Choose one of these two approaches, and write the reason in the manifest comment:
+- Run the agent in process over an `InMemoryTransport` pair, with the FoundationModelsACPAgent library product.
+- Start the `acp-agent` executable through `AgentProcess`. If you choose this approach, find how the binary gets built for the nested package (`integration-root-products` builds only root products, so this can need another approach).
+
+Use greedy decoding or the smallest real model that the agent repo uses in its own integration tests, so that each run gives the same result.
+
+Minimum tests, each through `ConnectionModel` and `SessionModel`:
+- `connect` and `initialize` give `ConnectionState.connected` and the agent capabilities.
+- `newSession` adds one `SessionModel` to `openSessions`. A second `newSession` adds a second model after the first.
+- `prompt` on a session gives a `UserMessageEntry` whose `sendState` becomes sent, and at least one `AgentMessageEntry` with text in `transcript`.
+- `close(_:)` (when the agent can close sessions) or `disconnect()` empties `openSessions` and marks each model closed.
+
+Give each test a time limit (`.timeLimit`).
+
+## Do not
+- Do not move the existing fast unit tests out of the root suite.
+- Do not select tests with an environment variable.
+- Do not add a busy state, a turn state, or an event stream.
+
+## Acceptance criteria
+- [ ] `IntegrationTests/Package.swift` exists and `swift test --package-path IntegrationTests` passes locally.
+- [ ] `swift test` at the root passes and runs no integration test.
+- [ ] `ci.yml` gives `integration-package-path: IntegrationTests` and the correct other inputs, with an updated header comment.
+- [ ] The stale `IntegrationTests/Package.resolved` is regenerated or removed as the new package needs.
+- [ ] After the push, the CI integration job runs (not `skipped`) and passes.
\ No newline at end of file
